SMTO-WEB-0002 — That web address can't be used

GUID: 2528a2ed-a147-4fba-bd6b-b50e907ba680
Slug: web-invalid-url
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use the web address it was given because it isn't a complete http or https address, it is too long, or it has a username or password written into it. Nothing was read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In your message, write the full address as it appears in your browser's address bar, starting with https:// or http://. The web reader only opens complete http or https addresses.
  2. Remove any username or password from the address, such as the part before an @ in https://name:password@site.com. SMTO's web reader never sends sign-in details inside an address and refuses addresses that contain them.
  3. If the address is very long, use a shorter link to the same page, for example without tracking text after the ?. Addresses longer than about 2,000 characters are refused.
  4. Check for typos in the site name or port number, such as spaces, missing dots or a port above 65535. A malformed site name or port makes the address invalid.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the page and shows its title or content in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address you meant to use, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't put passwords in web addresses to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Web URL validation rejected the address: it is not a string, exceeds the length limit, is not an absolute HTTP(S) URL, contains user credentials, or has a malformed host or port.

What this means

  • URL canonicalization rejects an invalid type, excessive length, unsupported scheme, embedded credentials, malformed host or invalid port. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • URL canonicalization rejects an invalid type, excessive length, unsupported scheme, embedded credentials, malformed host or invalid port.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original URL components and allowed scheme without exposing embedded credentials.

How to fix it

  • canonical_url in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/transport.py requires a string of at most 2048 characters (8192 for non-public provider calls) that passes gateway_core.http_contract.validate_url, with no userinfo; the fragment is dropped. Supply a valid absolute http(s) URL; use the HTTP connection tools when authenticated access is needed.
  • Provide a valid absolute URL using a supported scheme.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported absolute URL passes validation before network dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not insert credentials into the URL or keep submitting an invalid URL.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
